title: Open a biology talk
objective: Start a talk with a clear question and a plan the audience can follow.

slides.title: Give listeners a reason to listen
body: Greet the audience. Name the topic in familiar words.
State a question the audience can remember. Preview two or three parts of the talk.

slides.title: Listen to an opening
body: “Hello. Today I will talk about leaves in our garden. Why do some leaves have more holes?”
“First, I will show the two sites. Then I will compare the leaves.”
Ask a partner to say the speaker’s question in their own words.

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: You will speak about birds at a campus pond. Your talk will cover where you watched, what you saw and one question for next time.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Write a greeting and a title for your talk.
Say why you are giving the talk in one sentence.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: You will speak about bees in a campus garden. Your talk will cover where you watched, what you saw and one question for next time.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Write a greeting and a title for your talk.
Say why you are giving the talk in one sentence.
Give a three-part plan. Say the full opening to a partner.

slides.title: Try the opening again
body: Ask a listener to name the question and the next section. Change one line if either was unclear.
